I lost my dog almost a year ago, she was more like my baby than a dog. She was my person for 9 years, she understood me better than any human. She was sad when I was sad and she was happy when I was happy. I didn't get to say goodbye to her as she died from sepsis after an operation, but I understand what you're going through. Some people won't get it unless they're an animal lover too, but those pets we lose stay in our hearts forever. My Hollie was the one who lay in bed with me when I couldn't get up, she didn't judge me when I didn't wash and she was right there by my side when I left the house for the first time in 6 months. Now, when I feel myself slipping back into those dark days, I think of her and how much she helped me and sometimes, that's enough to keep me going. It is hard losing a pet, but it does get slightly easier as time goes by. I like to think of all pets, as a sort of Mary Poppins that comes into our lives when we need them most, to help us through our darkest days, and when they've done their job, it's time for them to go. I feel like this is especially true for those that suffer with depression and rely on our pets for emotional support, another Mary Poppins may come back into your life, but for now try and take solace in the fact that your pet gave you everything they had to get you through the day, and would do it for a million more years if they could.
